clues.text: This town is in the Northern Cape province of South Africa. It sits on the banks of the Orange River.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside South Africa's Northern Cape and the Orange River

source.quote: Upington (Khoekhoe: ǁKhara hais) is a town founded in 1873 and located in the Northern Cape province of South Africa, on the banks of the Orange River.

clues.text: The land is very dry, but the soil near the river is rich and good for crops. Fruit grows there in fields that get extra water.
clues.narrowing: rules out wet regions; points to dry river land where farming needs extra water

source.quote: The landscape is very arid but the soil is fertile and crops such as fruit are grown in irrigated fields.

clues.text: It was first a mission station, in eighteen seventy one. Reverend Christiaan Schröder was the man who ran it.
clues.narrowing: narrows to places that began as a mission station in 1871

source.quote: It originated as a mission station established in 1871 and run by Reverend Christiaan Schröder.

clues.text: A museum here holds a statue of a donkey. It thanks the hard work these animals did to help build up this dry region long ago.
clues.narrowing: narrows to the town whose museum thanks donkeys with a statue

source.quote: The museum is also the home of a donkey statue, which recognises the enormous contribution that this animal made to the development of the region during the pioneering days of the 19th century.

clues.text: This place is best known for fine grapes, raisins, and wines. They grow on the rich flood plains of the Orange River.
clues.narrowing: confirms a dry river town famed for grapes, raisins, and wines

source.quote: The area is best known for its export-quality grapes, raisins and wines, which are cultivated on the rich flood plains of the Orange River.
